summary: Playbook keywords override command-line options and configuration; within a playbook the more specific level (task over block/role over play) wins, as shown with the connection keyword. Keywords are distinct from variables.
questions: If I set connection at the play level, can one task use a different connection?
Which wins: a keyword set on the play or the same keyword set on a task?
Do playbook keywords override CLI options?
What is the difference between a playbook keyword and a variable?

answer_card.title: Playbook keyword precedence and inheritance
answer_card.answer_md:
Playbook keywords override command-line options and config settings. Within a playbook, the more specific level wins:

- play (most general)
- blocks / includes / imports / roles
- tasks (most specific)

```yaml
- hosts: all
  connection: ssh
  tasks:
    - name: Uses ssh
      ping:
    - name: Uses paramiko
      connection: paramiko
      ping:
```

Everything inherits play-level keywords, and any task, block or role can override them. Remember keywords are not variables: keywords describe how the playbook runs, variables are data.
